topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the learning objectives for understanding what causes cancer.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental nature of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease while evaluating the relative contributions of intrinsic mutations, environmental exposures, and geographic epidemiology to cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogens such as viruses and bacteria drive oncogenic processes, illustrated in detail by the etiology and mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical compounds undergo direct action or metabolic activation to form DNA adducts and mutations in specific tissues.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, microenvironment, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on the two-stage model of tumour promotion, chronic inflammation, and the role of host developmental stage in cancer risk.

topics.label: Approaches to identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to detect carcinogenicity and assess human exposure risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic brings the lecture to a close with a high-level summary of the main points on environmental carcinogenesis and risk assessment.
